The computer was looking for a single errant zero. If it found just one, then the Riemann\hhypothesis would fall apart. In the end, of the 10 trillion zeros that the computer checked, every single one was on the critical line. But if you see a pattern holding again and\h again and again, it's still impossible for machines to check it all the way to infinity. So\hbrute force computation will never resolve the Riemann hypothesis. That means there's\hstill only one way to be sure of it, and it's the same way that the ancient Greeks did\h their math: rigorous absolute mathematical proof.
